title: Platform economics and resilience sprint kickoff
summary: Quarterly health check focused on rising inference costs on checkout/recommendation traffic, intermittent latency regressions during promos, and alignment on a 3-week resilience + cost optimization sprint. Agreed pilot tests: burst-to-dedicated routing, KV cache tuning, and quantized model trial. Action owners and a follow-up benchmark demo scheduled.
next_steps: Redwood: share updated cost forecast and capacity plan (Daniel) by 2026-05-18
Clearwave: provide production traffic slice and synthetic promocy checkout traces by 2026-05-17
Schedule 60m benchmark demo with Clearwave engineers week of 2026-05-25
CSM to open pilot workspace and invite Clearwave team
action_items: Daniel Ortiz - produce 7-day capacity and cost model for checkout flow - due 2026-05-18
Leah Park - upload anonymized promo-day traffic sample to shared S3 link - due 2026-05-17
Priya Shah - create pilot workspace and grant roles for Clearwave engineers - due 2026-05-16
Tom Reyes - confirm internal stakeholders for decision meeting (CTO + FinOps) - due 2026-05-20
transcript:
Meeting start: 2026-05-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Daniel Ortiz, Priya Shah (Redwood) / Leah Park, Tom Reyes, Samir Patel, Jenna Liu, Oliver Grant (Clearwave)

Summary block (auto):
- Usage up 3.8x on checkout inference over last 90 days driven by marketing promos.
- Cost per 1k tokens trending up due to tail-latency and repeated cold cache lookups.
- Agreed pilot: route promo traffic to dedicated pool, enable prefix/KV cache for recommendation model, trial 4-bit quantized variant for non-critical ranking stage.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is maya from redwood, and we'll run through a quick QBR + sprint kickoff, um, want to make sure we align on costs and reliability.
00:12 Leah Park: hi, thanks. jumping in, we saw a cost spike last promo, uh, nearly doubled our inference bill week over week which caught finance off guard.
00:21 Oliver Grant: yeah that surprised us. it looked like per-request tokens were steady but e2e latency and retries skyrocketed.
00:30 Daniel Ortiz: right, from the traces we looked at there are a bunch of cold kv cache misses and also the model variant fallback triggered during high concurrency which increased tokens and dup requests.
00:44 Tom Reyes: can you explain that fallback? we were expecting host to handle bursty traffic.
00:48 Daniel Ortiz: sure, so when the hosted pool hits its autoscale limits we have a policy that routes to a cheaper capacity tier or a compat model. the compat model uses a longer context window and sometimes emits more tokens, so cost goes up. during promos you hit that threshold.
01:05 Leah Park: so dedicated capacity would avoid the fallback? is that guaranteed?
01:08 Daniel Ortiz: dedicated reduces the chance, yes, you get reserved throughput. not strictly "guaranteed" for infinite headroom, but you can provision buffer and burst capacity. also you get lower median latency.
01:18 Jenna Liu: what's the step for us to trial dedicated? budget and timeline are main blockers.
01:22 Maya Chen: we usually run a 2–3 week pilot: a reserved pool with defined commit for that window, plus canary routing of promo traffic. we'll share forecasted costs so you can compare to current spend.
01:33 Samir Patel: curious about on-prem options — data residency isn't the issue, it's that our infra team prefers VPC-attached endpoints and KMS integration.
01:40 Priya Shah: Clearwave can absolutely use Redwood Private for VPC and KMS; for this pilot we recommended staying hosted but with VPC peering and customer-managed keys if you want.
01:50 Oliver Grant: the other big ask from finance: show delta if we enable 4-bit quantization on the ranker — how much cost savings and any quality delta.
01:57 Daniel Ortiz: we can run A/B on accuracy vs latency. our bench shows 20–35% token-cost reduction on ranking with int4 for many models, but results vary by prompt and length. we should run your sample traces.
02:12 Tom Reyes: ok. technical deep dive — can you walk through the cache approach again? the precedence of KV vs prefix?
02:18 Daniel Ortiz: yeah so our system supports prefix caching and explicit KV cache for session keys. for recommendations, prefix caching helps when the same prompt prefix (cart + user features) repeats; KV is better for reusing key-value attention caches across beams. usually prefix cache is lower risk to deploy.
02:35 Leah Park: what's the ops story when cache warms? we saw a surge of misses on the first hour of promo which correlated with latency spikes.
02:44 Daniel Ortiz: adding a warmup job before the promo is one option — run fan-out warmers to prepopulate caches; another is adaptive batching thresholds to prioritize critical paths during warmup.
02:56 Priya Shah: that's in our playbook. also want to bring up observability: can you show token-level cost breakdowns per route?
03:04 Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Console has per-route token and latency breakdown. we'll export a promo-day view and include token-per-call and retry counts.
03:12 Oliver Grant: perfect. also need audit logs for billing reconciliations.
03:15 Priya Shah: we can include request-level logs and upload retention settings — you mentioned SOC 2 controls?
03:20 Maya Chen: yes, SOC 2 Type II is available. we also support SSO/SAML and RBAC in the console. we'll link the security package in the follow-up.
03:28 Tom Reyes: what about SLA on latency? the current SLO of 95th 250ms — that didn't hold during peak.
03:34 Daniel Ortiz: we can propose a canary and runbook: during a drop below SLO we auto-shift promo traffic to dedicated pool and then fall back gradually. that'll reduce retries and token inflation.
03:44 Leah Park: how do we measure success? what are the KPIs for the 3-week sprint?
03:49 Maya Chen: proposed KPIs: 30% reduction in promo-day per-request token cost, 40% reduction in 95th percentile latency during promos, and zero unplanned failovers. open to adjust.
04:00 Oliver Grant: finance will also look for absolute monthly burn delta.
04:04 Daniel Ortiz: we'll include that in the cost forecast.
04:08 Jenna Liu: any legal or compliance blockers for the dedicated pilot?
04:12 Maya Chen: nothing unusual — pilot paperwork is standard; for KMS you'd share key policy and we can confirm encryption-at-rest and in-transit.
04:20 Samir Patel: ok if we start with hosted + VPC peering then move to dedicated if numbers look right?
04:25 Maya Chen: that sounds like a good rollback-safe approach. we'll set thresholds.
04:29 Priya Shah: operational question: who is on-call from your side during the promo test?
04:33 Daniel Ortiz: we'll assign an SE with pager coverage for the trial window and give you the runbook.
04:38 Leah Park: can we get a dry-run this Friday? not the full traffic but the warming steps and routing rules validated.
04:42 Maya Chen: yes we can do a dry-run. we'll propose Friday 2026-05-15 14:00 UTC, pending your confirmation.
04:50 Oliver Grant: that works for finance to observe.
04:53 Tom Reyes: quick question about fallback model variants — are prompts preserved? last time we saw hallucinations increase.
04:57 Daniel Ortiz: fallback sometimes uses a larger context variant or a different tokenization which can change outputs. part of the sprint is to pin fallback behavior and test regressions with your eval set.
05:12 Maya Chen: ok let's recap action items and owners. (murmurs)
05:18 Priya Shah: I'll spin up the pilot workspace and invite Clearwave engineers; Daniel will prepare cost model and bench plan; Leah will provide traffic and evaluation prompts; Tom to confirm stakeholders; Maya to send security pack and draft SOW.
05:35 Maya Chen: perfect. we'll follow up with calendar invites and a baseline benchmarking doc.
05:42 Leah Park: thanks, appreciate the clarity — given the cost pressure we need a quick turnaround.
05:47 Maya Chen: absolutely. any final questions?
05:50 Oliver Grant: just one — what is the expected delta in median latency for dedicated? ballpark.
05:54 Daniel Ortiz: median usually drops 10–30% depending on workload; 95th sees largest gains because you avoid noisy neighbors and cold starts.
06:03 Tom Reyes: okay thank you, talk soon.
06:06 Meeting end: 17:02 UTC

Referenced artifacts / links: shared: https://redwood.ai/pilots/clearwave/cost-forecast (redwood link), security pack: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 (redwood link), benchmark template spreadsheet (shared in chat).

Recap (auto): Pilot plan: 3-week resilience & cost sprint: week 0 dry-run (cache warm & routing smoke test), week 1 routing to dedicated pilot + KV tuning, week 2 quantized ranker A/B and quality evaluation. Decision meeting 2026-05-28 to decide expansion or rollback.

End of transcript.
